## Why visit

A compact city-centre local with the cask depth of a dedicated beer destination. The two rooms and tiled passage make this a particularly good antidote to large modern bars, while the changing selection encourages a comparison of bitter, pale ale and a dark beer if available. It belongs near the top of a traditional Manchester route because it offers a substantial beer reason to visit as well as historic detail. Weekday lunch is a useful opportunity to experience it before the busiest evening sessions.

## Beer

CAMRA records eight handpumps, mostly rotating beers, with a mild often available and a vegan cask option documented. Ask what is freshly tapped rather than relying on a historic beer list.

## Food

## Plan the visit

Small rooms can fill quickly on Friday and Saturday evenings. Food timing is narrower than pub hours.

**Getting there:** Near St Peter’s Square tram stop; combine with Peveril of the Peak and Britons Protection.
